name: minspec
description: Complexity-adaptive specification-driven development. Classifies changes into tiers and applies proportional ceremony — a one-line fix needs one sentence of spec, an architecture rewrite gets the full treatment.

minspec.specsDir.description: Directory for spec files (relative to workspace root)

minspec.decisionsDir.description: Directory for architecture decision records (relative to workspace root)

minspec.specsLayout.description: How spec files are stored. 'flat': one file per spec (specs/SPEC-NNN-slug.md). 'spec-kit': one directory per spec with separate spec.md/plan.md/tasks.md — strict GitHub Spec Kit compatibility.

minspec.codelens.enabled.description: Enable/disable CodeLens annotations showing spec requirement mappings

minspec.conformance.enabled.description: Auto-export traceability when ScroogeLLM is detected (for conformance checking)

minspec.scroogellmNudge.enabled.description: Show ScroogeLLM installation suggestion when not installed

minspec.autoBootstrap.enabled.description: Auto-detect missing initialization, harness drift, and unclassified changes — and offer to run setup/refresh/classify. Per-prompt 'Don't ask again' choices are persisted in .minspec/preferences.json.

minspec.manualCreate.enabled.description: Show the manual 'Create Decision' / 'Create Epic' (+) buttons in the Decisions view toolbar. Off by default: with an AI assistant you normally create decisions and epics by asking it. Turn on for air-gapped / LLM-off (Tier-0) work, where the manual buttons are the primary way to author them.

minspec.autoClassifyOnCommit.description: Automatically run 'MinSpec: Classify Task Complexity' after each git commit (watches .git/HEAD and .git/refs/heads/*). Off by default.

minspec.commitOnApprove.description: When you approve a spec or accept a decision/epic (e.g. via Alt+A), commit the flipped document and the approval record together in one dedicated commit — so 'committed ground truth' is actually committed, never left sitting in the working tree. Pathspec-safe: only the approval's own files are committed, never other staged changes, and it refuses to commit in a detached HEAD. The commit runs your git hooks; it never pushes. Turn off to leave approvals staged for you to commit manually.

enumDescriptions: Never push. Approvals stay local until you push them yourself (fully offline).
Offer to push after each approval commit. Your click is the consent — nothing leaves the machine until you approve it.
Push automatically after each approval commit. Choosing this setting is itself the consent.
minspec.pushOnApprove.markdownDescription:
After an approval is committed (see `#minspec.commitOnApprove#`), get it to the remote so a sign-off cannot be stranded on one machine.

If the current branch is **protected** (see `#minspec.protectedBranches#`), a direct push would be rejected — so MinSpec instead creates a branch at the *same commit*, pushes that, and gives you a link to open the PR. Your checkout is never switched and no branch you are on is rewritten.

A push is a network call, so the default is `prompt`: nothing is sent until you click.

enumDescriptions: Open the pull request for you, labelled for the docs-lane so it auto-merges — the approval finishes with no extra click.
Show a notification with an 'Open PR' link and the compare URL, and let you create the PR yourself. This is the behaviour from before this setting existed.
minspec.approvalPr.markdownDescription:
What MinSpec does **after** an approval commit has already been pushed to a side branch because the current branch is protected (see `#minspec.pushOnApprove#` and `#minspec.protectedBranches#`).

- `auto` (default) — MinSpec runs your own authenticated `gh` to open the PR and applies the `docs-lane` label, which is what lets the lane workflow auto-merge it. The label is applied **only** when every committed path is docs (specs/, docs/, .minspec/approvals/, skills/*.md, top-level *.md); the workflow re-verifies this independently and refuses loudly otherwise, so code can never ride the lane.
- `manual` — the previous behaviour, exactly.

This setting **never causes a push of its own**: it only ever runs on a branch `#minspec.pushOnApprove#` already pushed with your consent, so with `pushOnApprove` at `never` — or a declined prompt — nothing here runs at all.

If `gh` is missing, not logged in, or GitHub is unreachable, `auto` degrades to exactly the `manual` notification with the reason appended. The approval is already committed and pushed either way.

minspec.protectedBranches.markdownDescription:
Branches that reject a direct push (branch protection / required PR). Used by `#minspec.pushOnApprove#` to push an approval on a new branch for a PR instead of attempting a push that would be rejected, and by the harness commit offer to avoid depositing a commit that could never be pushed. Read from settings rather than probed, so the decision needs no network call.

This default is the single source of truth: the generated pre-commit hook reads the git-config twin `minspec.protectedBranches` and falls back to the same three names, so all three guards agree.

minspec.autoBackfillUseAi.description: Always use the AI pass when backfilling epics (skips the per-run 'AI-enhanced?' prompt). Set globally by choosing 'Always' on that prompt — a personal preference that follows you across projects. Runs 'claude -p' locally; the extension makes no network calls. Off by default.

minspec.advancePhaseOnApprove.description: Always enqueue a phase-advance request when you approve a spec (skips the per-approval follow-up prompt). Set globally by choosing 'Always' on that prompt — a personal preference that follows you across projects. Enqueue-only: writes a request to .minspec/queue/ for a downstream consumer to dequeue; never runs 'claude -p' itself. Off by default.

minspec.approverEmail.markdownDescription: Your **explicit human identity** for recording approvals (DR-056). When set, approving a spec records this email as `approvedBy` instead of the ambient `git config user.email`. Use it when a checkout's git identity is an agent/bot (so approvals aren't refused as agent self-approval) while still attributing the human act to you. Leave blank to fall back to `git config user.email`. An agent/bot or blank identity is always refused — an approval must be an explicit human act. Personal preference; follows you across projects.

minspec.ruleset.requiredChecks.description: EXTRA status-check contexts the post-init branch-ruleset advisory requires, on top of the ones MinSpec resolves automatically. Empty by default: MinSpec already requires 'MinSpec SDD validation' (always produced by its own scaffolded CI), and adds 'ai-review'/'ready-to-merge' once their workflows and reviewer secrets are present, and 'lint'/'test'/'build' once package.json has a runnable script for them. Anything listed here is required VERBATIM and is never checked for producibility — a context no CI reports permanently blocks every PR on the default branch (#559).

minspec.coverage.minimumPercentage.description: Recommended minimum code coverage percentage. This setting only sets the pre-selected value in the 'MinSpec: Initialize SDD Structure' onboarding prompt (e.g. set it in a committed .vscode/settings.json to encode a team policy) — it does NOT itself change an already-initialized project's enforced threshold. The value CI and vitest actually enforce lives in .minspec/config.json's coverage.minimumPercentage; change an existing project by editing that file directly, or by re-running the onboarding prompt.

steps.title: Welcome to MinSpec
steps.description:
MinSpec brings Specification-Driven Development (SDD) to VS Code. Classify tasks by complexity, write just enough spec, and ship with confidence.

**Ceremony proportional to complexity** — a one-line fix needs one sentence of spec. A new subsystem gets the full treatment.

steps.title: Initialize Your Project
steps.description:
Set up the `.minspec/` directory, specs folder, and default configuration.

[Initialize SDD Structure](command:minspec.init)

steps.title: Classify Your First Task
steps.description:
Every task gets a complexity tier (T1-T4) that determines how much spec to write. The classifier suggests — you decide.

[Classify Task](command:minspec.classify)

steps.title: Explore the Sidebar
steps.description: The MinSpec panel in the Explorer sidebar shows all your specs, their tiers, phases, and task progress. The status bar tracks your active spec at a glance.

steps.title: Integrate with AI Tools
steps.description:
Inject your active spec context into CLAUDE.md, .cursorrules, or other AI tool configs. Keeps AI suggestions aligned with your specification.

[Inject Context](command:minspec.injectContext)
